text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Serbian parliament speaker Dragan Tomic and prime minister Mirko Marjanovic join in numerous official congratulations to President Slobodan Milosevic on the permanent lifting of international sanctions, praising him for succeeding in safeguardiing peace and lives of citizens.
- The world recognises benefits of Belgrade's peaceful policy, says editorial.
- Yugoslav businessmen say door to world market is now wide open after lifting of sanctions by U.N. Security Council.
- Partizan of Yugoslavia and Elan Bearnais of France playing in Belgrade tonight in match of European basketball champion's league.
- Sanctions have been lifted against Yugoslavia but the "outer wall" of sanctions for international financial institutions still remains, says commentary from Washington.
- EU commissioner Hans Van Den Broek says the union would propose granting same trade concessions to Yugoslavia as those applied to other states of the former Yugoslavia.
- Money supply in August was 35 percent up on December last year, say members of the banking committee of the Yugoslav Chamber of commerce.
- Metal workers' trade union Nezavisnost plans to organise protest gathering in front of Serbian government building today.
- As a first result of the lifting of sanctions Yugoslavia takes equal part in the UNESCO Paris meeting on education, with its proper seat and name plate.
- "We can say with satisfaction that the most difficult period is behind us," says federal government, referring to lifting of sanctions.
- Registration of parties for the federal elections expires at midnight on Thursday. -- Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 43 05
